newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bureaucracy holding up $2 bln for mining.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bureaucracy holding up $2 bln for mining.

text.p: Delays in approvals of mining concessions in Venezuela have held up about $2 billion which could be invested over the next five years if 300 pending applications were passed, a leading mining executive said Wednesday.

"There is $2 billion held up waiting for environmental permits to work in Venezuela," Pedro Tinoco, president of the Venezuelan Mining Chamber (Camiven) told a news conference with foreign correspondents.
Tinoco said about half of Venezuela's annual gold output of 14 to 15 tonnes is produced by small-scale miners operating without permits.
The mining chamber estimates between 40,000 and 60,000 illegal miners are operating in Venezuela's southern Bolivar and Amazonas states, he said.
Government officials have set a goal of raising Venezuela's gold output to 50 tonnes per year by the next century.
"It could be as high as 100 tonnes per year but they have to allow production," Tinoco said.
